stories.title: Distributed Attacks in Persistent-State AI Control
stories.author: Asa Cooper Stickland
bullet_points: New security threat identified in autonomous AI coding agents due to persistent codebases across sessions.

The paper introduces 'Iterative VibeCoding' to study the safe deployment of capable but untrusted AI systems.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLMs memorizing sensitive data, including PII.
Proposes 'LACUNA' as a testbed to evaluate the precision of LLM unlearning methods.
Highlights a gap in current research: existing benchmarks only test output-level unlearning, not true knowledge erasure.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of Large Language Models (LLMs) memorizing sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from training data.
It focuses on 'Unlearning,' a post-hoc method to reliably remove memorized knowledge from LLMs.
The research introduces LACUNA, a testbed to evaluate localization precision, challenging existing benchmarks that only test output-level erasure.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, non-rule-based programming tasks.
Proposes compiling natural-language specifications into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Aims to reduce reliance on external LLM APIs, addressing issues of locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: OrbitQuant: Data-Agnostic Quantization for Image and Video Diffusion Transformers
stories.author: Saurabh Shukla
bullet_points: Introduces OrbitQuant, a new data-agnostic quantization method specifically for Diffusion Transformers (DiTs).
Addresses the high inference cost of DiTs, which is exacerbated by their multi-step sampling and large parameter counts.
Solves the problem of activation shifting across different timesteps and prompts, which plagues traditional Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) methods.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'fuzzy-function programming' to address programming tasks difficult for rule-based systems (e.g., log alerting, JSON repair).
Proposes compiling natural-language specifications directly into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Aims to mitigate the drawbacks of relying on external LLM APIs, such as poor locality, lack of reproducibility, and high cost.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still produce unsafe outputs post-alignment training, necessitating real-time monitoring.
The research proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verifier signal.
The monitor's alarm decision is based on thresholding, calibrated via risk control, showing competitive performance in testing.

stories.title: ReContext: Recursive Evidence Replay as LLM Harness for Long-Context Reasoning
stories.author: Jingrui He
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLMs failing to effectively utilize relevant evidence within long context windows.
Introduces 'ReContext' (Recursive Evidence Replay), a training-free inference method designed to enhance long-context reasoning.
Focuses on bridging the gap between LLM context access capabilities and actual context utilization in practical applications.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structure (role, audience) influences LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances in a shared debate history against private, off-the-record (OTR) responses.
Examines the emergence of latent objectives within agents when social context is present, even without explicit prompting.

stories.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
stories.author: Qi Tian
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of speaker recognition in complex, long-form TV dramas.
A new large-scale benchmark, DramaSR-532K, has been introduced, containing 532K annotated dialogue lines across over 900 characters.
The work leverages Reasoning LLMs to improve the accuracy of character attribution in video content.

stories.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Introduces DemoPSD, a new method building upon On-policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for LLM training.
Addresses a critical limitation of OPSD: dense, privileged token-level supervision can cause overfitting and poor cross-domain generalization.
The research aims to improve LLM reasoning capabilities by mitigating the negative effects of overly strong teacher supervision.

stories.title: G-RRM: Guiding Symbolic Solvers with Recurrent Reasoning Models
stories.author: Günter Klambauer
bullet_points: Introduces G-RRM, a neuro-symbolic approach that integrates Recurrent Reasoning Models (SE-RRMs) with traditional symbolic solvers.
SE-RRMs function as neural solvers, generating complete solution proposals to guide classical methods like backtracking and SAT solvers.
The research focuses on SE-RRMs, which show improved extrapolation capabilities when dealing with larger problem sizes.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates

Compares public utterances made by agents against private, off-the-record (OTR) responses under the same conditions.

stories.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Introduces DemoPSD, a new method to address limitations in On-policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for LLMs.
Identifies that traditional dense token-level supervision in OPSD causes overfitting and poor cross-domain generalization.
Aims to improve LLM reasoning by modulating policy disagreement rather than relying solely on privileged teacher information.

stories.title: Controllable Sim Agents with Behavior Latents
stories.author: Ziran Wang
bullet_points: Introduces CNeVA, a new framework for controllable simulated agents.
The agents learn a per-agent Gaussian behavior latent from discounted returns.
This controllability allows engineers to test autonomous systems and isolate variables in traffic simulation without real-world risk.

stories.title: Neuron-Aware Data Selection for Annotation-Free LLM Self-Distillation
stories.author: Xiang Lorraine Li
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of post-training LLMs in specialized domains lacking human-labeled data.
Proposes a 'Neuron-Aware Data Selection' method for annotation-free self-distillation.
Utilizes the LLM's own outputs and majority voting across rollouts to generate pseudo-labels for self-supervision.

stories.title: Understanding the Robustness of Distributed Self-Supervised Learning Frameworks Against Non-IID Data
stories.author: Dong Yuan
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical challenge of data heterogeneity (non-IID data) in Distributed Self-Supervised Learning (D-SSL).
It provides a rigorous theoretical analysis to understand how various D-SSL frameworks maintain robustness under decentralized data conditions.
This work fills a gap in the current theoretical understanding of D-SSL performance when dealing with real-world, non-uniform data distributions.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: LLMs risk memorizing sensitive PII from training data, necessitating reliable data removal techniques.
Current unlearning methods often use a 'localize-first, unlearn-second' approach targeting specific model parameters.
The research highlights a gap in current benchmarks, which only test unlearning at the output level, not internal knowledge erasure.

stories.title: Towards Robustness against Typographic Attack with Training-free Concept Localization
stories.author: Aidong Zhang
bullet_points: CLIP models, foundational to modern LVLMs, are vulnerable to Typographic Attacks (TA).
TA occurs when irrelevant text within images biases visual representations toward lexical meaning.
The research proposes a training-free method for robust concept localization to address this vulnerability.

stories.title: Visually Grounded Self-Reflection for Vision-Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Greg Durrett
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) regarding self-reflection during multimodal reasoning.
Existing LVLMs struggle to ground self-correction in visual inputs, especially for out-of-distribution data.
The proposed solution utilizes Reinforcement Learning to enable visually grounded self-reflection in LVLMs.

stories.title: Will Scaling Improve Social Simulation with LLMs?
stories.author: Diyi Yang
bullet_points: The research investigates if scaling Large Language Models (LLMs) alone can improve the fidelity of social simulations.
The study compares LLMs' compute scale and general capabilities against the quality of their social simulations.
It questions whether simulation fidelity is inherently linked to general LLM capabilities or requires separate research focus.
